event.canonical_title: US Ambassador Visits Palestinian Town Affected by Settler Violence
event.summary: US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee visited the Palestinian town of Turmus Ayya in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, which has faced repeated violence from Israeli settlers. During his visit, Huckabee emphasized the need for the Israeli government to address the issue of violent settlers.

event_overview.title: About West Bank Violence
event_overview.subject: West Bank Violence
event_overview.summary: West Bank violence refers to a continuing pattern of confrontations and attacks in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, including violence involving Israeli settlers, Israeli security forces and Palestinians. The selected developments focus on attacks affecting Palestinian communities and a diplomatic visit, within a wider context of casualties, property damage, access restrictions and displacement.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: The event concerns the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, which United Nations bodies and the International Court of Justice treat as part of the Occupied Palestinian Territory.

facts.label: What “settler-related violence” covers
facts.value: OCHA defines settler-related incidents as violence, intimidation or trespass carried out by or against Israeli settlers and other Israeli civilians in the West Bank; its data can include deaths or injuries, property damage, and some intimidation or trespass incidents.

facts.label: Monitoring
facts.value: OCHA has systematically recorded settler violence since 2006. For incidents targeting Palestinians, it draws on sources including local authorities, Palestinian coordination offices, UN agencies, civil-society organizations and media, and generally validates incidents through at least two independent reliable sources.

facts.label: Humanitarian impact
facts.value: By the end of August 2026, OCHA had documented more than 1,600 settler attacks causing Palestinian casualties or property damage across 275 Palestinian communities that year; OCHA also identifies settler attacks and related access restrictions as a leading driver of displacement in the West Bank.

facts.label: Legal context
facts.value: In its advisory opinion of 19 July 2024, the International Court of Justice addressed the legal consequences of Israel’s policies and practices in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem. The Court’s opinion is part of the international legal context frequently cited in reporting on settlements and related violence.

event_overview.scope_note: This Muninn timeline highlights selected September 2026 developments, including a diplomatic visit and a reported killing, rather than providing a complete record of West Bank violence, settlement activity, military operations or legal and diplomatic responses.
